correctness.rationale: For beta=0 the spaces coincide. For beta!=0 set tau=2pi/|beta|, F=Fix(T_tau). Gluck 2021 Theorem 3.1 makes F a Dedekind-complete Banach lattice in its inherited order and norm, without requiring it be a sublattice of E. Restrictions U_s=T_s|F and U_{tau-s} are positive inverse operators, hence lattice automorphisms; choose a/tau irrational. Eigenvectors of U_a with eigenvalue exp(i j beta a) must satisfy U_t x=exp(i j beta t)x by density of nonnegative irrational multiples mod tau and strong continuity; their right derivative yields A x=i j beta x. Thus the eigenspaces agree for every integer j. Apply Gluck 2015 Proposition 3.1(b), whose normalized lattice-power/independence proof compares dimensions of an eigenvalue and its powers. For L1(T) plus L1(T) translations at speeds 1 and 2, Fourier modes give dimension 1 at i and 2 at 2i. This proves exact finite geometric multiplicity inequality, not generalized or approximate eigenspace claims.
residual_risks: The argument uses the exact inherited order on F; replacing it by lattice operations of E would be invalid.
Infinite dimensionalities are collapsed by convention and comparison does not preserve different infinite cardinals.

value.rationale: A finite geometric-multiplicity upgrade of the established cyclicity theorem directly answers the structural question Gluck 2021 left open for semigroups, and the explicit strictness example shows the inequality has quantitative content beyond eigenvalue existence. A precise reusable fixed-space/sampling lemma bridges discrete lattice homomorphism theory and continuous generators, making the result substantive without claiming broader spectra or a new cyclicity theorem.
residual_risks: Assumption of contractivity and Fatou lattice completeness is essential; no arbitrary C0-semigroup generalization claimed.

final_claim: For a positive contractive C0 semigroup on a monotonically complete Fatou complex Banach lattice, every imaginary generator eigenvalue i beta has eigenspace dimension <= that for i k beta for all integers k, counting all infinities as infinity; strictness can occur.
limitations: Generator geometric eigenspaces only; no approximate, algebraic or full spectral cyclicity.
Strong continuity is essential in density-to-eigenvector identification.
